about: Skill data for SkyWright's _geometry-harness/evalreport.py: the section order of a report, the sentence each finding kind is rendered with (placeholders are bound to the finding's own numbers and names, never free text), the grouping key, and the abridgement ladder concise mode walks when the print exceeds its page limit. The compiler reads this file; it decides nothing the file does not state.

sections.title: New regressions
sections.lead: A supplied combination with a new physical defect on any probe is a regression whatever its repaired counts say; repairs on one probe never net against a defect on another.

sections.title: Required checks with no accepted result
sections.lead: Each row keeps the evaluation incomplete. A check listed here was not measured on that arm; nothing about it is known from this bundle.

sections.title: Findings on each arm
sections.lead: One row per conflict group (check, kind, plugin A, plugin B) per arm and part. The differential verdict per probe is conflictdiff's own line, verbatim.

sections.title: Repaired and reclassified counts
sections.lead: Repaired only when a physical predicate went Holds to Gone; a row that changed hands with the defect intact is reclassified. These counts are never netted against a regression.

sections.title: Completed checks with no finding
sections.lead: No finding in the completed check, with the coverage the probe declared. The strongest sentence a null result supports is that the completed check found nothing in what it judged.

sections.title: Catalogues
sections.lead: Rows that are evidence, not defects. A catalogue completes its check and is never a finding.

sections.title: Media not assessed
sections.lead: Media is evidence only when its configuration fingerprint equals an accepted receipt's on that arm. Anything else is listed here and illustrates nothing.

sections.title: What was not assessed
sections.lead: Everything the disposition lists under unassessed, verbatim. Absence from the findings above is not a result for anything listed here.

prediction.about: The report leads with the prediction (what adding the evaluated mods will break), then coverage (what the checks could not judge), then validation against the patch. Only clashes between mods are predicted: a pair with a base-game file on one side, one mod against itself, overwrite history, or a clash already present without the evaluated mods is counted in setAside and kept in the machine record.

prediction.identityAbout: Checks whose row is a state of its own object (hanging, left without support): two setups show the same clash when the same object is in that state, whatever host or support the probe names as the cause. Other geometry rows are the pair of objects; record rows are the plugin pair, record and field.

oneSidedKinds.about: A kind of row that pairs two neighbouring records, whose words say when only one side differs from the base game (the other side's plugin carries the base game's value there and made no change of its own): such a row is one mod against the base game, never a clash between the two plugins it names (Missives review, blocking 2). Pattern per kind, matched on the row's words.

stateKinds.about: A world-state row's kind names the state it was found in (a quest stage or switch). One object against the same other object in several states is one clash, counted once and said with the number of states. The clash is the pair of objects (coordinator ruling on Pilgrim's blind review): an object sunk into another mod's object with both mods is a different clash from the same object sunk into a base-game object with one mod alone. `byObject` lists the state kinds identified by their own object instead; none is.

install.some: The patch fixes {hits} of {total} of these problems and leaves {left}.

readerDoc.patchSetsFields: Of the {total} changes above that one mod loses to the other, the patch sets {sets} to a value of its own choosing and leaves {left} as they are; whether its choice is the one you want is a matter of taste, so this page does not count them as fixed.
readerDoc.patchLeaves: It does not change the {n} {units} that come from {mod} alone.
readerDoc.patchNone: It causes no new problem of its own in the checks that ran.

order.forced: The order of these two mods is not a choice: {first} is flagged as a master file, so the game always loads it first. The patch loads after both.
order.forcedMaster: The order of these two mods is not a choice: the other mod lists {first} as a master, so {first} must load first. The patch loads after both.
order.free: Neither mod has to load first. This page describes the order that was tested ({first} first); the other order was not checked.
order.unknown: Whether the order of these two mods matters was not checked.
order.freeBoth: Neither mod has to load first, and both orders were checked: {count} changes in the game go to the other mod when the order is swapped. With {first} first, {measured}; with {second} first, {reversed}. Neither order is better on its own.
order.lostNone: nothing either mod changed is thrown away
order.withPatchNot: With the patch installed, the order no longer matters for these changes.
order.withPatchMatters: With the patch installed, {count} of these changes still depend on the order.
order.geometry: Where objects stand and where people can walk were checked in both orders too: {count} of those problems appear in one order only.
order.geometryNone: Where objects stand and where people can walk were checked in both orders too: none of those problems appears in one order only.
